haiku-low.q1: They see the same generic message as everyone else, saying a link was sent. Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request gets the generic message, with no commit changes, no new link and no email. The earlier links stay usable.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes. It ends sooner if used by a successful reset, or invalidated by a newer link or a failed queue or send.
haiku-low.q4: It is still usable. The password check fails before any link change, so it stays usable until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None stay logged in, since all sessions are deleted, including this device. The user logs in at the login page with the new password; no session is created.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times, then logs the failure, invalidates the link, raises an alert and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and only its hash is stored. The raw token is placed in the queued email job, which the worker sends in the /reset?token=T link.
haiku-low.q8: The server hashes the token with SHA-256, finds the row by unique token_hash, then checks it is not used, not invalidated and not expired.
haiku-low.q9: In password_reset_tokens, counting the account's rows from the last hour, using the user_id and created_at index. Rows older than an hour are deleted.
haiku-low.q10: Inside the transaction, after the limit check passes and before inserting the new link, older usable links get invalidated_at set.
haiku-low.q11: Password hash replaced, link used_at set, and sessions deleted, all in one transaction. The password-changed email is queued after that commit.
haiku-low.q12: Each submit locks the link row with SELECT FOR UPDATE and rechecks it. The second waits, sees it used, and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same generic reply (same text and status code, padded to a fixed minimum time). Nothing is written and no email is sent.
sonnet.q2: The fourth request within a rolling hour (cap of 3 links) gets the generic message. No new link and no email; the transaction commits with no changes, and the older link stays usable.
sonnet.q3: A link works for 30 minutes. It ends sooner if it is used (successful reset), or invalidated (a newer link is issued, or the email cannot be queued or sent).
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still usable (until it expires). The user gets a form error and nothing is written.
sonnet.q5: None. All sessions rows for the user are deleted, so every device is logged out, including the current one. No session is created; the user is redirected (303) to the login page and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with growing waits, then logs the failure, marks the link invalidated, raises an alert, and drops the job. The user is not told; they already saw the generic message. Failed sends still count toward the hourly cap.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated randomly (32 random bytes, sent as 43 URL-safe characters) and put in the email job on the queue; the email contains /reset?token=T. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in Postgres. The document does not say exactly where in the request flow the raw token is placed into the job, beyond the job containing the link.
sonnet.q8: It computes h = SHA-256(T) from the token in the URL and looks up the password_reset_tokens row by token_hash. The link is good if it is usable: not used, not invalidated, and not expired. Otherwise the expired page is shown.
sonnet.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table, which is counted for links issued to the account in the last hour (rolling 60 minutes, via created_at, index on (user_id, created_at)). Rows with created_at more than 1 hour old are deleted by the retention rule.
sonnet.q10: Inside the transaction, after the user row is locked and after the hourly-cap check passes (count under 3), the account's older usable links are invalidated (step 5), and then the new link is inserted (step 6), before COMMIT. A rate-limited request invalidates nothing.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: users.password_hash is set, the link's used_at is set, and all of the user's sessions rows are deleted. The password-changed email job is queued after the COMMIT (step 10), and if that fails the reset still stands.
sonnet.q12: The token is checked again inside the transaction with a row lock on the link row (FOR UPDATE). The first submit proceeds; the second waits for the lock, then sees the link used (used_at set), rolls back, and gets the expired page.
